These sources of air pollution would be short-term and limited to the period of construction. Applicant proposes to adhere to air pollution control regulations applicable to Oconee County and the State of South Carolina. Permits and operating certificates would be secured when required. Fuel-burning equipment would be kept in good mechanical order to minimize emmissions.
Noise levels would be expected to increase during construction due to blasting, machinery operation, and other related construction procedures. Some of these noises would be audible from the upper Whitewater Falls area and from Lake Jocassee and would have an adverse effect on wildlife in the vicinity. The effects of construction-associated noise would be short-term in nature.
3.1.5 Waste Disposal
Most waste materials generated by construction would be solid wastes such as timber and brush from reservoir clearing, scraps and forming lumber, and miscellaneous trash. Applicant proposes to dispose of all construction wastes by incineration or burial in a local landfill in accordance with applicable regulations. Spoil materials would be placed in the designated spoil area to the east of the upper reservoir site.
Incineration of wastes would result in the liberation of large quantities of smoke into the air. This smoke would reduce the ambient air quality in the upper reservoir and neighboring areas. In addition, smoke from burning could have an adverse impact on the scenic and aesthetic quality of nearby Whitewater Falls, an important visitor attraction.
Hard rock excavated from the underground tunnels and powerhouse area would be used in the construction of an underwater weir in the Whitewater Arm of Lake Jocassee, about 1,600 feet downstream from the Bad Creek outlet structure. Any excavated rock in excess of the needs of weir construction would be either used in the dam in the form removed, crushed for use on temporary project roads, disposed of in designated spoil areas, or a combination of the above.
